# Configuration reference

Every key wedge accepts, generated from the JSON Schema that wedge validates
against (print it with `wedge schema`). Unknown keys are rejected, so a typo is
an error rather than a silently ignored setting. For explanations and worked
examples, see the [user guide](README.md).

## `[server]`

Process-wide server settings (`[server]`).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `admin` | table (see below) |  | Admin listener for metrics and reload. Off unless set. |
| `debug` | table (see below) |  | Debug capture of every request. For troubleshooting only; never in production. Restart-only. |
| `default_vhost` | string | unset | Name of the vhost that answers requests whose Host matches no vhost. When unset, such requests get 421 Misdirected Request. |
| `limits` | table (see below) |  | Resource limits; the defaults are safe for an internet-facing server. |
| `listen` | list of string | `[]` | Addresses to listen on, such as `"0.0.0.0:80"` or `"[::]:443"`. |
| `listen_tls` | list of string | `[]` | Addresses that accept TLS connections, such as `"[::]:443"`. Needs at least one vhost with a `[vhost.tls]` certificate. |
| `tls` | table (see below) |  | TLS protocol settings shared by all TLS listeners. |
| `trusted_proxies` | list of IP address or CIDR range |  | Peers (such as a load balancer in front of wedge) whose `X-Forwarded-For` wedge extends instead of replacing (T4.6). |

## `[[upstream]]`

A group of backend servers for the reverse proxy (`[[upstream]]`). See the threat model, Phase 4.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `connect_timeout_secs` | integer (1 to 300) | `5` | Seconds allowed to open a TCP connection to a server. |
| `health_interval_secs` | integer (1 to 3600) | `10` | Seconds between health checks. |
| `health_path` | string | unset | Path probed with GET to check each server, such as `"/healthz"`. Without it, servers are only marked down when connections fail. |
| `name` | string | **required** | Name that `[[vhost.proxy]]` routes refer to. |
| `response_timeout_secs` | integer (1 to 3600) | `30` | Seconds allowed for a server to send its response head. |
| `servers` | list of string | **required** | Backend addresses as IP:port (no host names, so no DNS rebinding, T4.3). Requests go to healthy servers in turn. |
| `unhealthy_after` | integer (1 to 100) | `2` | Consecutive failures (checks or connection errors) that mark a server down. One success marks it up again. |

## `[[vhost]]`

A virtual host (`[[vhost]]`).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `follow_symlinks` | boolean | `false` | Serve files reached through symbolic links. Off by default; even when on, the resolved file must still lie inside `root`. |
| `headers` | table of name = string |  | Extra response headers, such as `"Content-Security-Policy"`. A value replaces a default security header of the same name; an empty value removes it. |
| `hosts` | list of string | `[]` | Host names this vhost answers, such as `"example.com"` or `"*.example.com"` (any subdomain). Matching ignores case and port. |
| `name` | string | **required** | Unique name used in logs and diagnostics. |
| `proxy` | list of table (see below) |  | Reverse proxy routes, checked before static files. |
| `root` | string | unset | Directory served for this host. Optional when the vhost has proxy routes; requests that match no route then get 404. |
| `tls` | table (see below) |  | Certificate for TLS listeners. Without it, this vhost is not served on TLS listeners. |

## `[server.admin]`

The admin listener (`[server.admin]`): `GET /metrics` and `POST /-/reload`. See the threat model, T5.1 to T5.6.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allow` | list of IP address or CIDR range |  | Client addresses allowed to connect. Defaults to loopback only. |
| `listen` | string | **required** | Address of the admin listener, such as `"127.0.0.1:9900"`. Keep it off public interfaces. |
| `token` | secret reference: `"env:NAME"` or `"file:/path"` |  | Bearer token required for `POST /-/reload`, as a secret reference (`env:NAME` or `file:/path`). Without it, reload over HTTP is off. |

## `[server.debug]`

Debug capture (`[server.debug]`). See the threat model, T5.9 to T5.12.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `capture_file` | string | `"capture.log"` | Capture log path; relative paths are relative to the master file. |
| `keep_files` | integer (1 to 100) | `5` | Rotated files kept (`capture.log.1` ...). |
| `log_secrets` | boolean | `false` | Write credentials (`Authorization`, `Cookie`, `Set-Cookie`, `Proxy-Authorization` and `redact_headers`) unredacted. Breaks the "secrets never reach logs" rule while on. |
| `max_bytes_per_connection` | integer (0 to 1073741824) | `65536` | Bytes recorded per connection and direction; the rest is counted only. |
| `max_file_bytes` | integer (65536 to 17179869184) | `104857600` | Size at which the capture log is rotated. |
| `read_packet` | boolean | `false` | Write a capture log with each connection's bytes at every layer wedge sees (TCP, TLS, HTTP, routing), each step tagged with the source file that handled it. |
| `redact_headers` | list of string | `[]` | More header names to redact, besides the built-in ones. |
| `tcp_headers` | boolean | `false` | Also record IP/TCP packet headers (sequence numbers, flags, window, retransmits) through pcap. Needs a build with the `packet-capture` feature, libpcap or Npcap, and root/admin or CAP_NET_RAW. |

## `[server.limits]`

Connection and request limits (`[server.limits]`). See the threat model, entries T2.5 to T2.8.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `h2_max_concurrent_streams` | integer (1 to 1000) | `100` | Maximum concurrent HTTP/2 streams per connection. |
| `header_timeout_secs` | integer (1 to 300) | `10` | Seconds allowed to receive a complete request head, including the wait for the next request on a kept-alive connection. |
| `idle_timeout_secs` | integer (1 to 3600) | `60` | Seconds a connection may go without any bytes read or written before it is closed. Covers clients that connect and never send a request. |
| `max_connections` | integer (1 to 1000000) | `1024` | Maximum simultaneous client connections across all listeners. |
| `max_header_bytes` | integer (8192 to 1048576) | `16384` | Maximum bytes buffered for an HTTP/1 request head, and maximum HTTP/2 header list size. |
| `max_headers` | integer (1 to 1000) | `100` | Maximum number of request headers. |
| `max_uri_bytes` | integer (256 to 65536) | `8192` | Maximum request-target (URI) length in bytes. |
| `request_timeout_secs` | integer (1 to 3600) | `30` | Seconds allowed for a handler to produce a response head. |
| `shutdown_grace_secs` | integer (0 to 3600) | `30` | Seconds to let in-flight requests finish after a shutdown signal. |

## `[server.tls]`

TLS protocol settings (`[server.tls]`). See the threat model, T3.1.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `min_version` | `"1.2"` or `"1.3"` |  | Lowest TLS version offered. Versions below 1.2 are not supported. |

## `[[vhost.proxy]]`

Sends requests under a path prefix to an upstream (`[[vhost.proxy]]`).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_body_bytes` | integer (0 to 4294967296) | `10485760` | Largest request body accepted, in bytes (T4.7). |
| `path` | string | **required** | Path prefix starting with `/`, such as `"/api/"`. `"/api"` matches `/api` and `/api/...` but not `/apix`. The longest prefix wins. |
| `upstream` | string | **required** | Name of the `[[upstream]]` that serves this route. |

## `[vhost.tls]`

A vhost's certificate (`[vhost.tls]`). Both values are secret references (`env:NAME` or `file:/path`); relative file paths are relative to the master configuration file.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cert` | secret reference: `"env:NAME"` or `"file:/path"` | **required** | PEM certificate chain, leaf certificate first. |
| `hsts_include_subdomains` | boolean | `false` | Add `includeSubDomains` to HSTS. Only enable when every subdomain serves HTTPS. |
| `hsts_max_age_secs` | integer (0 to 63072000) | `31536000` | `Strict-Transport-Security` max-age on TLS responses; 0 turns HSTS off. |
| `key` | secret reference: `"env:NAME"` or `"file:/path"` | **required** | PEM private key (PKCS#8, PKCS#1 or SEC1). |
| `redirect_http` | boolean | `false` | Answer plain-HTTP requests for this vhost with a 308 redirect to the first TLS listener. |
